title: Vespasian
lead: The Roman general who was running the war in Judea when Nero died, became emperor on 1 July AD 69, and began the Flavian dynasty. His son Titus ended the siege of Jerusalem in AD 70.

sections.b: Josephus says Nero, troubled by the Roman defeat in Judea, chose Vespasian as the one man able to bear so great a war, and sent him to take command of the armies in Syria (Jewish War 3.1.1-3). Wikipedia gives his birth as 17 November AD 9, his consulship as 51, and his reign as 1 July 69 to 23 June 79. Tacitus first mentions him at 1:10: he is running the war in Judea with three legions, has no plan against Galba, and had sent Titus to greet him.
sections.refs: Histories of Tacitus 1:10; Histories of Tacitus 1:46; Histories of Tacitus 1:76

sections.b: Vespasian was proclaimed at Alexandria on 1 July 69 after Tiberius Julius Alexander, the prefect of Egypt, had the legions swear to him (Tacitus, Histories 2:79, which gives 1 July; Josephus, Jewish War 4.10.6). Tacitus says Vespasian began his own career (1:1). Josephus became his client after being taken at Jotapata, where he said he had foretold Vespasian's rise (Wikipedia, Josephus).
